query: Magneto-Raman spectroscopy of bilayer or few-layer CrI3: how do Raman intensities change at the layered antiferromagnetic to ferromagnetic spin-flip transition in magnetic field?

hits.text: Unlike  the  monolayer,  bilayer  CrI3  hosts  either  a  ferromagnetic-like  state  or  a  layered antiferromagnetic state, depending on the applied magnetic field, below a critical temperature of 45 K. Figure 3a shows the low-frequency Raman spectrum of a CrI3 bilayer in an applied field of 6 T. Since the magnetization of both layers are aligned in the same direction by the magnetic field, the bilayer essentially behaves like a ferromagnetic monolayer. That is, the acoustic magnon mode is  cross-circularly  polarized  with  the  Stokes  and  anti-Stokes  peaks  showing  opposite  selection rules and shifts linearly in energy with a g factor of ~2.1 under applied field (Fig. 3b). However, in  contrast  to  the  monolayer,  we  observe  switching  of  acoustic  magnon  modes  as  the  bilayer undergoes  a  metamagnetic  transition  between  -0.7  T  and  -0.75  T  (see  Fig.  S4  for  RMCD measurements with consistent transition field). Figure 3c shows a series of Raman spectra as the magnetic states switch from the AFM to the FM-like state. Since the shift of the magnon peak over small  field  ranges  near  the  metamagnetic  transition  is  smaller  than  the  resolution  of  our spectrometer, we utilize Lorentzian fits to track subtle changes in the magnon energy (see Fig. S5). In the AFM state, at fields close to the metamagnetic transition, the acoustic magnon mode has a frequency of ~3.6 cm -1 . As the field passes the metamagnetic transition, the magnon mode at 3.6 cm -1 vanishes. Instead, another acoustic mode, starting at a lower frequency of ~3.0 cm -1 , appears and linearly shifts to higher energy as the magnitude of the field increases.

CrI3 is one of the most widely studied vdW magnetic semiconductors in recent years. T C of CrI3 varies between 61 K in the bulk form and 45K in the single monolayer limit. 17 In the bilayer form, CrI3 comprises of antiferromagnetically coupled FM layers with outof-plane magnetic anisotropy. When a sufficiently strong out-of-plane magnetic field ( l 0 H C > 0.5 T) is applied, spins flip such that spins in both layers align parallel to the field, resulting in AFM-FM transition. 17 Bilayer CrI 3 in the AFM state exhibits a linear magnetoelectric effect due to broken time-reversal and inversion symmetries. 72 The magnetoelectric coupling strength is enhanced near the spin-flip transition, but abruptly vanishes upon transition to the FM state due to restoration of inversion symmetry. Interestingly, when a constant magnetic field near the spin-flip transition is applied, a reversible AFM-FM crossover can be achieved by electric fields. 72 Other trihalides (e. g. CrBr 3 ), dihalides (e. g. FeCl 2 ), and some ternary chalcogenides (e. g. MnBi2Te4 and CrPS4) exhibit similar interlayer A-type AFM 73-76 order, but their magnetoelectric properties are largely unexplored.

hits.text: AFM-FM transition in bilayer CrI3 can also be induced by charge modulation. 77,78 With increasing electrostatic doping, interlayer exchange coupling is reduced until it vanishes; that is, the layers are magnetically decoupled. This occurs at the critical electron density of  2.5 -10 13 cm  2 , which can be readily achieved by a conventional solid gate dielectric. With a constant magnetic field near the spin-flip transition applied, reversible AFM-FM transition can be achieved by electrostatic doping. Charge modulation also affects the intralayer exchange coupling 79 in monolayer CrI3, leading to a modest decrease (increase) in T C (  10%) with injection of electrons (holes) at a density of  10 13 cm  2 (Ref. 77). Unlike the magnetoelectric effect, charge modulation also changes the saturation magnetization. These incremental changes can be attributed to the SE nature of magnetic coupling in CrI 3 which shows weak dependence on charge density. 80

The layer-dependent ground state of few-layer CrI 3 offers additional opportunities to study the effects of the magnetic state on the optical spectrum that are inaccessible in bulk. While the bulk is FM, the weak interlayer AFM coupling of few-layer CrI 3 allows a switching between layered AFM/FM states through metamagnetic transitions [18, 30-32]. We thus studied the magnetic field dependent MCD spectrum of 5L and 2L CrI 3 at T = 1 . 75 K shown in Fig. 5(a)/(b), respectively. The insets show the hysteresis at fixed E = 1 . 959 eV for each sample, confirming the field induced transition from AFM to FM stacking configurations at B c (5 L ) ∼ 1 . 8 T and B c (2 L ) ∼ 0 . 6 T. The 5L sample shows a remnant magnetization at zero field due to the odd layer number while the bilayer is nearly compensated at B = 0 T, consistent with previous reports [83].

hits.text: As we stated above, the magneto-optical Kerr effect firstly confirmed the existence of magnetism in atomically thin CrI3 sheets. 28 Remarkably, 2D CrI3 systems also exhibit magnetic response dependent on the number of layers. The magnetic ground states of monolayer, bilayer, and trilayer CrI 3 are FM, AFM, FM, respectively, while the magnetic ground state of 3D bulk CrI3 crystal is FM. The AFM interlayer coupling in bilayer CrI 3 is mainly due to structural transition 437 and super-superexchange interaction. 23 The TC of monolayer and trilayer CrI 3 is 45 and 61 K, respectively, meaning that the magnetic coupling is strengthened as the thickness of CrI 3 sheet increases. The dependences of TC/TN on the number of layers have also been found in the other experimentally fabricated 2D magnets, including Fe3GeTe2, 41,50 CrGeTe3, 37 FePS3, 48 and MnBi2Te4. 319 Unlike CrI3, there is no thickness-induced flipping of magnetic ground state in multilayer Fe3GeTe2, CrGeTe3, and FePS3 systems. However, their increasing trend with the number of layers behaves differently, which are more pronounced in Fe3GeTe2 and CrGeTe3. The TC of four- or five-layer Fe 3 GeTe2 is 220 K, dropping to 180 K for bilayer, and finally to 130 K for monolayer. 41 For CrGeTe3, the TC of bilayer and bulk phase is 41 and 66 K, respectively. In contrast, the value of TN in AFM FePS3 is not sensitive to the number of layers, with a fixed value of 118K. 48 In addition, the unique layer-dependent magnetism has also been found in MnBi2Te4. 319 The monolayer MnBi2Te4 is a topologically trivial ferromagnet, whereas the multilayer systems made up of odd and even numbers of layers are interlayer ferromagnets and antiferromagnets, respectively.

hits.heading_path: 5.1.1 Photoluminescence and reflectance/absorbance for studying two-dimensional magnetism
hits.text: Using few-layer CrI 3 as an example, its photoluminescence spectra feature a ligand field exciton peak at ∼ 1.1 eV. Its absorption/differential reflectance spectra resolve four peaks at ∼ 1.5 eV and ∼ 1.9 eV that result from the ligand field transitions from 4 A 2 to 4 T 2 and 4 T 1 , and at ∼ 2.2 eV and ∼ 2.7 eV that originate from the ligand-metal charge transfer transitions (Figure 19a) [276, 322]. The photoluminescence spectra show strong helicity dependence on the magnetic ground state; in the paramagnetic phase, there is no intensity contrast between σ + and σ -circularly polarized photoluminescence; in the FM state of monolayer CrI 3 , clear dichroism is observed between σ + and σ -circularly polarized photoluminescence whose relative strength depends on the FM magnetization orientation; in the layered AFM state of bilayer CrI 3 , equivalent spectra are detected in σ + and σ -circularly polarized photoluminescence channels; and in the layered FM state of bilayer CrI 3 above the spin-flip transition field, distinct spectra are shown between σ + and σ -circularly polarized photoluminescence (Figure 19b).
